Date of passing of impugned order 17.09.2024  [2024:RJ-JD:41648] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-12580/2024]
2.

It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that the victim 'P' has been examined in the trial as P.W.4 and it is noticed that the discrepancies are appearing in her statement recorded during trial and during the investigation.
She made several admissions in cross-examination which somehow support the case of the defence regarding consent.
Her assertion that there are some of the lines in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. were not told by her to the Magistrate gives rise to a reasonable doubts regarding her credibility.
This Court is not inclined to give any final opinion in this regard and the above observations have been made just for justifiable disposal of the bail application.
The issue with regard to age of the victim is to be determined by learned trial Court after close scrutiny of her academic record and documents related to her birth.
At this stage, when the victim has been examined there remains no apprehension that she may be hampered or her evidence can be tampered.
The petitioner is a young boy.

A perusal of the statement of Medical Officer P.W.1 - Dr. Kanchan Saini revealing that when she examined the victim, she found no signs of forceful resistance or violence and as a matter of fact no external injury was there.
3. Be that as it may, I do not deem it appropriate to extend further incarceration of the petitioner.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to him.

[2024:RJ-JD:41648] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12580/2024]
4. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
5.
I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.
There is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

6. Accordingly, the instant third bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused- petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 41-Ravi Khandelwal Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
